A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v2 references a separate supplementary file that is neither included nor embedded. v3 includes Appendices A–C, so some appendix material cannot be reliably classified as new versus previously supplementary.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on four text domains, human pairwise judgments, WildChat interactions and multi-round generation, including results in Figures 2–9.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional writing-style, human-validation, multi-round and text-detection results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The mutual-information/self-information measure, surrogate-model evaluation and output-only lower-bound estimator are retained. Equations (1)–(10) describe the same procedures. Revised threshold settings and expanded calibration documentation do not establish a different underlying method.

E1.justification: The four original creative domains and WildChat evaluation remain. v3 adds binary human-versus-AI text detection on CHEAT, HC3-English, HC3-Chinese and Ghostbuster, expanding language and domain coverage (C.6). Multi-round scenarios also expand beyond adding details to hallucination and grammar correction (C.5).

E2.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports evaluation against competing contribution measures or detectors. The additional generators in v3 are evaluation model configurations. Ghostbuster appears as a dataset in Table 2, not as an evaluated detector baseline; newly cited detectors likewise receive no comparative scores.

E3.justification: Human validation increases from 1,000 to 1,500 pairs. Reported estimator settings change from tau=0.65/0.7 to -log(tau)=0.5496/0.4155 for Llama-3/Mixtral. v3 adds Claude 3.5 Haiku and Gemini 2.0 Flash generation settings, controlled style/refinement protocols, and detection evaluation using 1,000 human and 1,000 AI texts per benchmark with ROC–AUC. These are reported setting changes, not proof that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a controlled four-style news experiment examining sensitivity to wording (Section 5.2, Figure 3). Its multi-round analysis expands from one detail-expansion scenario to four scenarios involving expansion, hallucination correction and grammar correction (C.5, Figure 15). Existing length, temperature and adaptive-attack analyses are retained in C.1–C.3.

E5.justification: Both versions report five generations per input. v3 documents three-annotator majority voting, 91.47% unanimous agreement and mean-plus-one-standard-deviation threshold calibration. Because v2's annotation and supplementary details are unavailable, whether these statistical practices were introduced or merely documented more explicitly cannot be reliably determined.

E6.justification: Human-ranking agreement changes from 97.4% to 95.93% with the expanded annotation sample, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. v3 additionally reports 92.87% agreement for output-only estimates. Table 2 adds AUCs of 0.9593, 0.9931, 0.9710 and 0.9857 for CHEAT, HC3-English, HC3-Chinese and Ghostbuster, respectively. Estimator distributions change under revised thresholds, and new style, generator and refinement results substantially extend the evidence.

T1.justification: The two contribution definitions, geometric-mean plausibility condition and lower-bound derivation remain mathematically unchanged. v2's estimator derivation moves to v3 Appendix B. Threshold-selection guidance adds empirical detail rather than a new theorem, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an information-theoretic contribution measure, validation across creative domains and an extension for unavailable human input. v3 foregrounds the extension in its abstract and contribution bullets, but v2 already states it in the introduction and develops it extensively. The central scientific contribution remains the same.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly cautions that informational contribution is not equivalent to creativity, originality or authorship. It adds interpretations of stylistic stability and the effects of hallucination and grammar correction, plus guidance on model- and domain-dependent threshold calibration. Existing modality, copyright and adaptive-attack limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: Confirmed changes include API identifiers for the added generators, prompts for added tests and explicit current threshold-calibration instructions. v3 omits v2's code-access link, hardware specifications and 0.33-second-per-sample timing. However, v2 assigns sampling, prompt and annotation details to its missing supplement, preventing a reliable assessment of the overall extent of new documentation versus relocation.

R1.justification: v3 adds detection references such as Binoculars, Learning to Rewrite and Wu et al.'s survey, alongside references for the added detection datasets and Gemini. Several general model and copyright references disappear. The central positioning of informational contribution measurement relative to binary AI-text detection is retained.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative into numbered Introduction, Related Work, Dataset Construction, Methods, Experiments and Conclusion sections. Methods move before experiments; the detailed estimator derivation and several analyses move to appendices. It adds contribution bullets and a contents page, separates Limitations, and rewrites the Discussion into a shorter Conclusion.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column layout to two columns. Generator grids expand from four to six columns, several domain plots are consolidated in appendix figures, and the multi-round figure expands from one scenario to four. v3 adds the style figure and detection table, redraws estimator plots with changed scales, and shortens captions, removing explanations of medians, quartiles, whiskers and outliers.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens support for the output-only estimator through human-ranking validation and more varied refinement tests, and clarifies the distinction between informational contribution and creative value. Its explicit calibration recipe also improves auditability. These gains support a limited net improvement, tempered by omission of v2's code-access and hardware/timing disclosures and uncertainty about the earlier supplementary documentation.
